short: The period of military rule during the Interregnum when England, Scotland, and Ireland were governed by a Lord Protector.
full:
Established in December 1653, the Protectorate was the constitutional arrangement that made Oliver Cromwell the Lord Protector of the Commonwealth of England, Scotland, and Ireland. Following the failure of the Rump Parliament and the short-lived Nominated Assembly, the military drafted the "Instrument of Government," Britain's first written constitution. It granted Cromwell executive power alongside a Council of State and a single-chamber parliament, effectively creating a quasi-monarchical military dictatorship.

Domestically, the Protectorate enforced Puritan social reforms, divided the country under the deeply unpopular rule of the Major-Generals, and readmitted Jews to England. Internationally, it pursued an aggressive foreign policy, building a formidable navy and securing victories against Spain. Following Cromwell's death in 1658, his son Richard briefly succeeded him but lacked military support, leading to the rapid collapse of the Protectorate and the restoration of the monarchy in 1660.
